findings.summary: ADR 0069's Consequences section states that an AUDIT_CHANGED verdict is recorded, but this slice records only AUDIT_UNCHANGED, so the durable decision record describes behavior the shipped tree does not have.
findings.evidence: docs/adr/0069-bounded-generator-self-audit-before-qa-dispatch.md:78-82 reads "until it exists an `AUDIT_CHANGED` verdict is recorded and changes nothing downstream", and :86-89 reads "the persisted outcome carries the candidate tree the audit was handed and the tree it left behind". src/self-audit.ts:190-196 guards the write with `if (classification.verdict === "AUDIT_UNCHANGED")`, and src/self-audit.test.ts:229-231 asserts the opposite of the ADR sentence: after an AUDIT_CHANGED run, `expect(selfAuditsFor(loadRunState(stateRoot, PRD_SLUG), GH_ISSUE)).toEqual([])`. Probe: `pnpm vitest run src/self-audit.test.ts` — 8 passed, including "reports AUDIT_CHANGED when the audit rewrote the tree", which passes precisely because nothing is persisted.
findings.expected: contract.md Non-goals: "Recording `AUDIT_CHANGED` or `AUDIT_NOT_RUN` in run state. This slice lands the persisted shape covering all three verdicts so neither sibling slice needs a second version bump, but only `AUDIT_UNCHANGED` is written here." The contract's own scope lock words the changed-tree case as "an `AUDIT_CHANGED` verdict is classified and returned but changes nothing downstream" — classified and returned, not recorded.
findings.observed: The ADR asserts as present-tense fact that AUDIT_CHANGED is recorded. On this tree it is classified, returned, and discarded; no run-state entry is written for it. B-11's declared observations (mechanism, swarm-forge provenance, swarm_handoff.sh, the one-invocation bound, ADR structure) are all satisfied, so this is an accuracy defect in the record rather than a missing behavior.
findings.clearCondition: ADR 0069's Consequences section describes the changed-tree case in terms that match the shipped stage — that an AUDIT_CHANGED verdict is classified and changes nothing downstream, with recording deferred to the sibling slice — and no sentence in the ADR claims a persisted entry exists for a verdict this slice does not write.

findings.summary: sanitizeSelfAudits — 50 lines of new load-time validation with a load-bearing whole-list-drops-on-one-malformed-entry rule — has no test, against a run-state convention where every other record sanitizer has one.
findings.evidence: src/run-state.ts:1028-1083 adds `sanitizeSelfAudits` with five reject branches (non-object container, non-array value, non-object entry, blank/absent candidateTreeId, unknown verdict, blank auditedTreeId) plus a whole-key discard on `dropped || entries.length === 0`. Neither test added for B-10/P-03 (src/run-state.test.ts:1185, :1220) feeds it a malformed entry: both write well-formed records through `recordSelfAuditOutcome`. The convention it departs from: src/run-state.test.ts:205 (collidingPrefixes), :275 (locators, #91 B-06), :498 (resume entries) and :951 (appliedWaivers, #193 B-13) each pin the malformed-record degradation. Probe: `pnpm vitest run src/run-state.test.ts` — 5 files, 210 tests, exit 0; deleting the verdict check from sanitizeSelfAudits would keep every one of them green.
findings.expected: acceptance-manifest.json B-10 lists "sanitization in adaptLoadedState" among the shipped members, and CLAUDE.md's "Where a new assertion goes" ranks a unit test as the first-choice home for a new assertion — which is exactly what this branch set is.
findings.observed: The sanitizer's behavior is unobserved. A regression that widened it (accepting an unknown verdict string, or keeping a partially-valid list) or narrowed it (rejecting a well-formed entry) would not fail any test in the suite. Mitigating: the sanitizer mirrors `sanitizeQualityStages` (src/run-state.ts:847) structurally and line for line, and that precedent is also untested, so this is convention-consistent rather than novel; and the contract's test plan does not name a sanitization scenario.
findings.clearCondition: A src/run-state.test.ts case loads a state whose selfAudits carries a malformed entry — an unknown verdict string or a blank candidateTreeId — and asserts the resulting degradation, so the sanitizer's reject branches fail a test when they change.
